title: File:2017 Total Solar Eclipse (AFRC2017-0233-008).jpg
author: NASA Armstrong Flight Research Center / NASA/Carla Thomas
description: During the total solar eclipse, the Sun’s corona, only visible during the total eclipse, is shown as a crown of white flares from the surface. The red spots called Bailey's beads occurs where the moon grazes by the Sun and the rugged lunar limb topography allows beads of sunlight to shine through in some areas as photographed from NASA Armstrong’s Gulfstream III. Photo Credit: (NASA/Carla Thomas)
